_comment: These are here because regex and AST cannot reach them, which is the whole
reason this pipeline exists alongside tools/golden_rules.py. A dead opcode
mask is `PAT & MASK != PAT` -- arithmetic, so a deterministic check finds it
every time. But 'this thread polls instead of parking' has no fixed spelling:
it can be a `while` on an atomic, a `loop` with a `yield_now`, a sleep-driven
deadline, or a lock re-taken every iteration. Same violation, different text.
That is what semantic retrieval is for, and the earlier version of this file
wasted it on things a grep already handled.
`pattern` is real code that actually shipped in this repository, pulled from
the commit where it existed -- not an invented example. The rule it breaks is
in `spec`; `fixed_in` is where it stopped breaking it.

exemplars.why: A component thread paces itself from the host clock. Spec 1.4 scopes wall-clock batching to the CPU cores alone; everything else must be driven by emulated cycles. This exact shape throttled Master SH-2 by two orders of magnitude (history.md Chapter 32) because the lockstep window followed the slowest reporter.
exemplars.fixed_in: Chapter 34 — V-Blank now comes from Sh2::step's own cycle count

checks.q: Does this code read the host clock (Instant::now, SystemTime) to decide WHEN to do work?
Is this inside the SH-2 CPU interpreter loop?

exemplars.why: A non-CPU thread loops on a condition and yields instead of parking. Spec 1.5: the only continuous loop in the system is the CPU's own; every other thread blocks on a Condvar until a real hardware event wakes it. Measured cost of this shape: 5 of 8 threads at 25-99% CPU on a black screen.

checks.q: Is there a loop that repeatedly re-checks a condition instead of blocking?
Does this code wait on a Condvar?

exemplars.why: A hardware timing signal -- the VBLANK flag a game polls -- derived from the host clock instead of emulated cycles. Spec 1.5: timing generators (VDP2 H-Blank/V-Blank, SCU timers) are driven by real Master SH-2 cycles, never a wall clock. Emulated time and host time drift apart the moment the host is loaded or the emulator is throttled, so the flag stops matching the interrupts the same code raises.
exemplars.fixed_in: Chapter 34 — Scu::advance_video_line, from Sh2::step's own cycle count

checks.q: Does this code derive a hardware status flag or interrupt timing from Instant::now or elapsed time?
Is the timing derived from a cycle counter?
